reportText: @ Canyon Mouth , 17 cfs @ Fort Collins , 3 c fs @ North Fork below Seaman Reservoir Winter is trying to move into the hills now that we are approaching then end of November. Cold nightime temperatures have been starting to leave ice covering stretches of the Poudre River in the canyon along with edge ice in town. Recent reports have let us know that much of the pools and slower water in the canyon are iced over in the mornings. Give the sun some time to warm up the surface to help break up some of the ice. Focus on the warm afternoons as your times to go fishing. Look for deeper pools that fish tend to congregate in and work these meticulously with a nymph rig. As far as the fishing goes, we are pretty much on our winter program with where are flows are at. The Poudre is running low and clear, so keeping your presentation small and running light tippet is key to success. Running a small dry dropper rig can be effective on the warmer days when fish are actively eating midges and blue wings. On those colder days, try running a deeper nymph rig with a small attractor like a prince nymph or rainbow warrior with a small midge or blue wing trailing behind. Stripping a small Thin Mint or Black Wooly Bugger has been a super fun way to find fish. If you have any questions or are interested in our winter classes, feel free to give us a call for the latest lineup of events.
